description: List Granola meeting notes, one page at a time. Filter by creation or update date and by folder, then page with the returned cursor. Returns metadata only: id, title, owner, created_at, updated_at. Only notes with a finished AI summary and transcript appear here — a meeting still being processed is absent. Read a note's summary with granola-read_notes-1 and its spoken lines with granola-read_transcripts-1.

created_after.description: Return notes created after this date. "2026-01-27" or "2026-01-27T15:30:00Z".

created_before.description: Return notes created before this date. "2026-01-27" or "2026-01-27T15:30:00Z".

updated_after.description: Return notes updated after this date. "2026-01-27" or "2026-01-27T15:30:00Z".

folder_id.description: Return notes in this folder and its child folders. Looks like fol_00000000000001.

cursor.description: The next_cursor from the previous page.

limit.description: Notes per page, 1 to 30. Granola defaults to 10.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as cursor to read the next page. Null on the last page.

response_schema.description: GET /v1/notes. Lenient on purpose. Granola's OpenAPI document marks most of these required, but a node that dies on a vendor's new null returns nothing at all.

quirks.why_execute: JSON-first definitions carry no declarative response-to-output mapping, and this node renames the provider's hasMore and cursor into has_more and next_cursor. That rename is the only code in execute.ts.
quirks.provider_ingress: The lenient JSON Schema ingress on the provider's own payload is response_schema above. The runtime compiles it and runs it on the way in; execute.ts only names the shape it guaranteed.
quirks.dates: Granola accepts a plain date (2026-01-27) or an RFC 3339 timestamp (2026-01-27T15:30:00Z). The node passes the string through and lets the provider judge it, rather than pinning a format the vendor may widen.
quirks.ordering: The OpenAPI document does not promise an order. The node does not claim one either.
